doc.title: Chris Parker interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 5, 2023

title: Paul Butterfield calls him in Woodstock: Better Days
summary: The fur-hatted man watching him in Woodstock turns out to be Paul Butterfield, who forms Better Days with Geoff Muldaur and becomes a paternal mentor.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: bunch of different groups. But there’s only, at that time there was only so many places to play in Woodstock and I always noticed this guy standing in the background with a fur hat, big fur hat, you could only see his face and he had this giant like an Eskimo fur hat on. And I thought you know it was a typical character in Woodstock, I had no idea it was Paul Butterfield and he had been checking me out in all these different contexts and then one day I got a call from him and I said, “Yeah, right” and I hung up. And I thought it was somebody putting me on. And he called right back and said, “No really, this is Paul Butterfield, I want to know if you want to do some playing” blah-blah-blah. And that’s how he inducted me. And this wasn’t the Paul Butterfield Blues band, this was a new thing that he wanted to put together with Geoff Muldaur. It ended up being called Better Days and we did two albums and then I did some other albums with him after that band broke up. But he was wonderful. Very paternal towards me, I was pretty young and he really encouraged me and I learned a lot playing with him, not to mention the other guys in the band. So that was — I just I don’t know why he chose me, I guess he liked what he heard.
